title_en: After Fan Backlash Over Typos and Bad Reprints Forced a Delay, What's Happened to Magic: The Gathering’s Monster Hunter Secret Lair?
summary_en: Where is the delayed MTG x Monster Hunter Secret Lair? Here is what happened to the postponed drop and what Wizards of the Coast is reworking.
body_en:
Magic: The Gathering has been running Secret Lair drops for a long time now, and we’re basically getting at least one per week in 2026 .
These limited drops have been contentious, to say the least. Wizards of the Coast can print to demand when it wants to, but other times it feels like it’s only scalpers and scammers that win out.
Still, purchasing mechanisms aside, there’s one Secret Lair drop I can’t stop thinking about: the Monster Hunter Superdrop.
Monster Hunter likely needs little introduction to you, the discerning IGN reader, but the action RPG franchise is one of my favorites and has been since 2018’s Monster Hunter: World.
As you can imagine, the announcement of a Secret Lair for the series, including the iconic monsters, weapons, and more from the game series, had me ready to hand over my card details before you could say Palico.
It's fair to say that I, like just about everyone else in the middle of the Magic: The Gathering x Monster Hunter Venn diagram, was more than a little let down.
The cards were uninspired and reprinted cards you could find for a few cents. Some even had typos, and the whole thing felt rushed.
“Let's cut to the chase: the Secret Lair x Monster Hunter™ Superdrop we revealed last week fell short of expectations,” Wizards of the Coast’s blog post explained .
“We heard loud and clear that you were disappointed, and we believe we can do better. So, we're going to postpone this release and rework this Superdrop entirely.”
The company went on to promise more information in 2026 , and noted that Capcom “is on board for us to take another swing at this Superdrop”, but it’s all been very quiet since.
Given we’re now into September, we’ve reached out to Wizards of the Coast to see if there’s any update.
Prior to being “reworked”, here’s what the set was offering:
The Hunt:
The Hunters:
The Monsters:
The Monsters II:
As a big Monster Hunter fan and Commander player, I’m really hoping one of these is an Ur-Dragon reprint as one of the franchise's biggest flying monsters. Having a five-color Commander would allow players to build a deck that includes everything in this Secret Lair drop, essentially building out a Monster Hunter-themed deck that would be great fun to play (even if synergies would be minimal!).
Here’s hoping it’s worth the wait - just like when Wizards teased a Destiny-themed Secret Lair.
